name: Fairshare Maintenance Visit Checklist
author: Keshav Grover

sections.description:
Fairshare Maintenance Visit Checklist replaces manual spreadsheet maintenance with a single, guided admin screen built for periodic maintenance visits (for example, every 2 to 3 months):

  • Zero Idle Overhead: Loads no front-end assets, sets no cookies, schedules no background cron jobs, and stores all data in non-autoloaded options so the site stays fast between visits.
  • Pre-Flight Gate & Fresh Sessions: Shows your Last Maintenance Visit summary and automatically resets ephemeral session checklists after 24 hours while preserving your permanent Log Book.
  • Fast Batched Before vs After Crawler: Uses the WordPress HTTP API (wp_safe_remote_get) in small 3-page batches with TLS verification and strict same-host checks to compare Reachable Pages, Sections, Menu Links, Hyperlinks, Images, Words, and Characters without hitting hosting timeouts.
  • Safe 1-by-1 Updates: Separates Core, Theme, and Plugin updates, verifies actual installed versions, preserves prior plugin activation state, and enforces target-specific multisite capability checks.
  • Maintenance Log Book & Flexible Sheets Export: Records technician name, date/time, before/after client changes timing, and structural counts, plus flexible Google Sheets copy/CSV export (with Website Name, Yes/No/All filtering, and optional site-check columns).

Built and maintained by Fair Share IT Services alongside our website monitoring and maintenance tooling at WebsitesWatch.
sections.installation:
1. Install Fairshare Maintenance Visit Checklist from Plugins -> Add New or upload the plugin zip.
  2. Activate the plugin and open Maintenance Visit in the WordPress admin sidebar.
  3. Confirm the pre-flight step, review the Before/After crawl, run updates 1-by-1, check users/posts/settings, save a Log Book entry, and export your CSV.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin affect front-end speed or Core Web Vitals?

No. It enqueues zero front-end CSS, JavaScript, fonts, or cookies, and stores all data in non-autoloaded options.

Does it send any data to external servers?

No. Everything runs locally inside your WordPress admin area using only standard WordPress update checks and same-site page verification.

What happens when I open the plugin again after 2 to 3 months?

Any checklist session older than 24 hours automatically resets so you start with fresh update lists and a fresh Before baseline, while your Maintenance Log Book history stays permanently saved.
sections.changelog:
3.2.1

  • Added a “Skip deactivated plugins” safety toggle (enabled by default) enforced in both the UI and REST API so inactive plugins are never accidentally updated or activated.
  • Added pre-update PHP and WordPress version compatibility checks (Requires PHP / Requires WP) to block incompatible plugin updates before touching files.
  • Added OPcache and file stat-cache flushing after upgrades plus a fatal-error shutdown guard that safely isolates broken plugins and releases the update lock if a third-party plugin triggers a compile/fatal error.

3.2.0

  • Added a Delete Controls Safety Lock (locked by default) with inline 2-step confirmation for deleting users, trashing posts, removing categories, and removing Log Book entries.
  • Added Website Name to Copy for Google Sheets & CSV exports, plus row filters (All / Only Yes / Only No / Only Yes & No) and toggles for Header Row and User/Post/Email check columns.
  • Improved UI/UX with a KPI overview strip, side-by-side Core & Theme cards, instant plugin search & status filter chips, and color-coded status banners.

3.1.2

  • Added smooth 3-page client-driven batched crawling (/crawl-init, /crawl-step, /crawl-finish) with live per-page progress so crawls never feel laggy or hit shared-hosting timeouts.
  • Added wp_raise_memory_limit('admin') and transient auto-refresh before plugin/theme upgrades for reliable heavy plugin updates.

3.1.1

  • Enforced target-specific activate_plugin / deactivate_plugin capability checks unconditionally before multisite network capability checks, and added target-specific capability checks to /quick-action.

3.1.0

  • Initial public release as Fairshare Maintenance Visit Checklist (fairshare-maintenance-visit-checklist).
